name: e2e_bead_capture_assay_c3: lyse, incubate, separate, wash
description: UNROUTED. Built by assay2chip/stages/s6_build.py from partition.json: ops 12 lyse, 13 lyse -> trap_chamber 'lyse_12', op 15 incubate -> trap_chamber 'incubate_15', op 16 separate -> trap_chamber 'separate_16', ops 17 wash, 18 lyse -> polygon_chamber 'wash_17'. lyse, mix, incubate, separate, wash share one board; they run between 4 and 25 C; 6 of the 6 ports allowed at demo scale; 46% of the envelope 30 x 20 mm (demo envelope), ONE fluidic layer at ONE 0.3 mm etch depth, base and lid 0.5 / 1 mm. COP (Zeonor 1060R) because hot_embossing route; 90 C max working temperature covers the 25 C hold; DNA adsorption Low: hydrophobic, little DNA binding; protein/enzyme adsorption possible. The hottest hold here is 25 C. SIZED FROM THE LOAD, never from the paper's tube volumes (assay2chip/README.md, 'Bench volumes do not transfer'): lyse_12 from 2,000 capsules at 1500 per uL = 1.33 uL of suspension (the largest load of op(s) 12, 13: op 12); incubate_15 from 2,000 capsules at 1500 per uL = 1.33 uL of suspension; separate_16 from a stated packed bed of 28.0616 uL; wash_17 from 2,000 cells at 1500 per uL = 1.33 uL of suspension (the largest load of op(s) 17, 18: op 17). ONE PART PER PLACE (chip/designs/README.md rule 1): ops 12, 13 (lyse, lyse) all act on the same capsules in 'lyse_12', so they share one chamber sized for the largest of their loads and held at each temperature in turn; ops 17, 18 (wash, lyse) all act on the same cells in 'wash_17', so they share one chamber sized for the largest of their loads and held at each temperature in turn. PLACEMENT: parts sit in flow order in 1 row(s) (left to right), spread across the usable 23.6 x 13.6 mm so the slack between them is routing corridor. Total chain length 64.4 mm, crossing risk 0, nothing rotated; every feature keeps at least 0.4 mm to its neighbours and to the chip edge. PORTS: 4 (inlet_1, outlet_1, reagent_in, waste), each over a PORT PAD the registry sized, so the bore opens entirely onto cut area and the port-overlap rule in tools/check_chip_spec.py passes. Inlets and outlets are on opposite edges, which is what keeps the layout planar in one layer, and no two ports are closer than 5 mm. CHANNELS BETWEEN PARTS ARE DELIBERATELY EMPTY: S7 routes them from assay2chip/work/<id>/connections_e2e_bead_capture_assay_c3.json. Until it has run, a chamber here is unconnected on purpose, and every rule that needs a channel - channel width against capsule diameter, channel crossings, protocol targets - can only be checked after S7. REALISED AS CHANNELS, not as parts: op(s) 14 (mix) - op(s) 14 (mix) carry a stream and nothing states a residence time, so there is no length or volume to build to; realised as the connecting channel rather than as a part. A conduit is sized from flow and residence time, and one that comes out smaller than a face a channel can attach to is not a small part but an unusable one, so it becomes the channel instead, lengthened to the length it needs. Parts sized by assay2chip/parts/registry.py. RISKS carried from sizing: Z TOLERANCE: the gap is 25 um and published z tolerance on these processes is +/-20 um, which is +/-80% of it, so the weir could close or leak outright. blocks.json calls this the biggest unknown in the retention scheme: coupon 21, 24 and 27 um gaps before committing. If it fails, the lever is capsule size (tunable 35-260 um), which buys a proportionally larger gap.; flow distribution across a wide weir is explicitly NOT scale-free (blocks.json target_envelope.not_scale_free); this crest is 2.11 mm wide; flow distribution across a wide weir is explicitly NOT scale-free (blocks.json target_envelope.not_scale_free); this crest is 9.67 mm wide.
